annotation.authors_or_issuer: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), U.S. Department of Transportation
named_instruments_referenced: Geneva Convention on the International Recognition of Rights in Aircraft
annotation.summary_en: The FAA's binding federal regulation (14 CFR Part 47) sets out how aircraft are registered in the United States. It covers who may register, what proof of ownership is needed, registration numbers, fees, how long a registration lasts and when it must be renewed, and dealer certificates. Drones are mentioned in only one provision, which requires manufacturer serial numbers for unmanned aircraft with remote identification.
key_provisions_or_claims: Aircraft may be operated only if registered by an eligible owner (U.S. citizens, resident aliens, qualifying corporations).
Unmanned aircraft registration must use manufacturer serial numbers compliant with Part 89 remote identification.
Certificates of Aircraft Registration expire after seven years and must be renewed.
Foreign-registered aircraft must show that the foreign registration has ended, under the Geneva Convention and the Cape Town Treaty.
Dealer's Aircraft Registration Certificates allow manufacturers and dealers to fly aircraft for flight tests and sales.
